subject: The one mistake 90% of users make with AI picks
preview_text: You're probably using the confidence scores wrong. This changes everything about winning.
body_paragraphs: I watched a guy at Cheltenham last week throw away £200 because he read the numbers backwards. He had the AI's top pick, the data was screaming at him, but he bet against it. Why? He saw the 78% confidence score and thought 'not good enough.' He wanted 90s. That's like turning down a winning lottery ticket because you wanted the jackpot.

Here's the truth the sharpest punters know: a 65% confidence score on Predictify isn't a C-grade. It's a license to print money. The AI isn't grading on a curve—it's calculating pure probability against the bookies' odds. A 65% pick where the odds are 3/1? That's value screaming your name. Most users chase the 85%+ unicorns and miss the consistent winners sitting right there.

Open the app right now. Pull up any race. Don't just look at the #1 pick. Look at the confidence score, then look at the odds. Your new rule: if the confidence is 10+ points higher than what the implied probability of the odds suggests, you've found gold. This is how you move from picking winners to finding value—the only thing that matters long-term.

Go to today's featured race and apply the 10-point rule to the top three AI picks. See which one the market has wildly mispriced. That's your bet. P.S.
